---
title: "Contributing to JedR Academy"
author: "Christian McDonald"
---

OK, to be honest, we haven't yet done any collaboration outside our little universe, so this is sparse and subject to change.

See the Installation section of the [project README](https://github.com/utdata/jedr-academy) for setup and information about Quarto Live.

Where we need the most help is in building new "Training" modules. You can look at [this github issue](https://github.com/utdata/jedr-academy/issues/2) for some ideas.

- **Fork the repository**: Click the "Fork" button on the project page to create a copy of the repository in your own GitHub account. 
- **Clone your fork**: Use Git command line to download your forked repository to your local machine. 
- **Create a branch**: Create a new branch from the main branch to isolate your changes. 
- **Make changes/create content**: Follow our styles. Look at the existing tutorials and trials. Follow the fun you find there.Put tutorials in the `tutorials/` folders and trials in the `trials/` folder.
- **Commit changes**: Save your changes with a descriptive commit message explaining what you modified. 
- **Push to your fork**: Upload your changes to your forked repository on GitHub. 
- **Open a pull request**: Initiate a request to merge your changes into the original project by creating a pull request. 

At that point we will review your pull request. We may ask for revisions, and eventually merge your changes if approved.
